prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Under `featureSingleAssetVault`, `MPTokenAuthorize::preclaim` already
rejects `tfMPTUnauthorize` on an individually-locked MPToken with
`tecNO_PERMISSION`. This PR extends the same guard so it also fires
when `fixCleanup3_4_0` is enabled

### API Impact

No public API, libxrpl, or peer protocol impact. The behavior change is gated
behind the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment.

## Test Plan

Tests: extend testSetEnabled to cover the four corners of the
(featureSingleAssetVault × fixCleanup3_4_0) matrix.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: Small, well-scoped change that extends the existing lsfMPTLocked unauthorize guard to also fire under fixCleanup3_4_0, mirroring the existing featureSingleAssetVault check. The test updates correctly gate the previous behavior on both flags being disabled and add the two missing corners (all-both, all-fixCleanup3_4_0) to complete the 2x2 amendment matrix. No correctness, security, or consistency issues found in the added lines.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: This is a small, well-scoped fix that extends an existing lsfMPTLocked/tfMPTUnauthorize guard in MPTokenAuthorize::preclaim to also fire when fixCleanup3_4_0 is enabled (previously only guarded by featureSingleAssetVault). The corresponding test file update correctly mirrors the new condition (skipping the 'delete despite locked' path when either amendment is on) and adds test invocations covering all four corners of the amendment matrix, matching the stated test plan. The logic change is simple, correct, and consistent with the described intent — no bugs, security issues, or missed instances of the pattern were found in the diff.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: The fix correctly decouples the locked-MPToken unauthorize guard from featureSingleAssetVault by adding a fixCleanup3_4_0 branch, and additionally teaches the new branch to tolerate a destroyed issuance (sleMptIssuance null) so a locked-but-orphaned MPToken doesn't become permanently stuck. The hoisting of the sleMptIssuance read to the top of preclaim is a safe, read-only refactor. The testSetEnabled additions correctly cover all four corners of the (SAV × fixCleanup3_4_0) matrix, but the new testLockedMPTokenDestroyedIssuance helper — which exercises the exact scenario this PR is about — is only invoked for 3 of the 4 corners, missing the 'SAV off, fixCleanup3_4_0 on' case that specifically proves the guard now fires independent of SAV.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: The change extends the locked-MPToken unauthorize guard to fire under fixCleanup3_4_0, and additionally makes that guard require the issuance to still exist (so a locked MPToken whose issuance was destroyed can be cleaned up once fixCleanup3_4_0 is enabled). This is a slightly larger behavior change than the title implies ('extend the check' vs 'extend the check + add issuance-existence gating'), but it is deliberately covered by the new testLockedMPTokenDestroyedIssuance test across all four feature-flag corners, and the refactor to hoist the single sleMptIssuance read to the top of preclaim() is a correct, behavior-preserving cleanup of the duplicated reads. No correctness, security, or resource-leak issues found in the diff.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: This change extends the existing locked-MPToken unauthorize guard (previously gated only on featureSingleAssetVault) to also apply when fixCleanup3_4_0 is enabled, and refactors MPTokenAuthorize::preclaim to hoist the repeated `sleMptIssuance` ledger read into a single lookup at the top of the function reused by all branches. The new fixCleanup3_4_0 branch additionally requires the issuance to still exist (`sleMptIssuance && locked`) before blocking, which intentionally allows cleanup of a locked MPToken whose issuance was destroyed — this is the exact scenario covered by the new testLockedMPTokenDestroyedIssuance test, and the four-corner (SAV × fixCleanup3_4_0) matrix is exercised in both testSetEnabled and the new test. I traced through the branch logic against the new/updated test expectations for all four amendment combinations and didn't find a discrepancy; the hoisting of sleMptIssuance is also behavior-preserving since the view is read-only within preclaim. No correctness, security, or resource issues found in the added lines.

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: ## Pull request overview This PR updates `MPTokenAuthorize::preclaim` so that unauthorize attempts against individually locked MPTokens are rejected not only under `featureSingleAssetVault`, but also when `fixCleanup3_4_0` is enabled—while still permitting cleanup of “dangling” locked MPTokens after an issuance has been destroyed under the fix. **Changes:** - Extend the locked-MPToken unauthorize guard to also apply when `fixCleanup3_4_0` is enabled (with an issuance-existence exception). - Expand `MPToken_test` coverage to exercise the `featureSingleAssetVault × fixCleanup3_4_0` behavior matrix. - Add a regression test covering behavior when a locked holder MPToken remains after its issuance is destroyed. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/test/app/MPToken_test.cpp | Adds matrix coverage for `testSetEnabled` and introduces a new regression test for dangling locked MPTokens after issuance destruction. | | src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/token/MPTokenAuthorize.cpp | Extends the preclaim locked-token unauthorize rejection to `fixCleanup3_4_0`, and refactors issuance lookup to be shared. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: This is a well-scoped fix that extends the existing locked-MPToken unauthorize guard to also apply under fixCleanup3_4_0, while additionally allowing cleanup of a dangling locked MPToken when its issuance has already been destroyed (a case the old SAV-only check could never resolve, leaving a permanently stuck MPToken). The refactor to read sleMptIssuance once at the top of preclaim is a safe deduplication (same keylet, same view, no behavioral change from moving the read earlier). The if/else-if structure correctly gives fixCleanup3_4_0 precedence over the legacy featureSingleAssetVault-only behavior, and the new sleMptIssuance-guard in the fixCleanup3_4_0 branch is deliberate — verified against the new testLockedMPTokenDestroyedIssuance test, which explicitly exercises the four amendment-combination corners and confirms the dangling-token cleanup path only activates when fixCleanup3_4_0 is enabled. I did not find correctness, security, or resource-management issues in the added lines; the accompanying test coverage (four-corner matrix in testSetEnabled plus the new destroyed-issuance test run across all four combinations) matches the implementation's branching logic.

### Context of Change

Adding a separate PR just to add the amendment makes it easier to manage separate/independent PRs that may require the amendment.
